Subject: Data access controls & support access  follow-up from today's call

Hi Daniel / Alice,

Thanks again for taking time today  appreciate the clear prioritization. Quick recap + action items so we can line up the next technical deep-dive: 

Summary from the call:
- Primary concerns: PII handling, retention policies (end-of-life/deletion), detailed logging for support access, and assurance around data residency.
- Must-haves: RBAC with least-privilege roles, SSO integration (SAML/SCIM), break-glass process for emergency vendor support that preserves auditability, and ability to BYOK for encryption keys.

Requested items (what we'll provide next):
1) Short security brief that maps our access controls to your checklist (attached).
2) RBAC role matrix and examples for common admin/ops/support roles  Dev will send this with technical specifics.
3) Break-glass runbook (how support access is granted, approval flow, and audit trail retention).
4) Confirmation of data residency options and retention/deletion mechanics for customer data.
5) SOC 2 Type II and pen test summary (we can share the redacted report).

Next steps / asks from you:
- Please confirm whether you require a formal BAA/contractual data processing addendum (we can loop legal), and any specific retention windows that differ from our defaults.
- Share any compliance portals or questionnaires you want us to fill out (e.g., your security vendor form).

Proposed timeline: Dev and I can run a 45-min technical deep-dive on Thurs 22 Jul or Fri 23 Jul  which works better for your infra/security lead?

Attachments: redwood-data-security-summary.pdf, SOC2_report_redwood.pdf

Thanks,

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the clear recap  this is helpful. A couple of clarifications from our side before we schedule the deep-dive: 

- Break-glass: We need to understand exactly what 'temporary support access' looks like. Specifically: who approves, how long access is granted, whether we get a full immutable audit trail, and whether sessions are recorded.
- Encryption/BYOK: We require key separation for customer data; can you confirm support for external KMS (AWS KMS or GCP KMS) and whether Redwood has access to plaintext keys in any workflow?
- Retention: Our baseline requirement is 90 days for logs and 1 year for any derived artifacts unless otherwise agreed. We also need an option to set shorter retention per dataset.
- Compliance artifacts: Please send SOC 2 Type II and an executive summary of penetration testing. If you have a security questionnaire template, please send and we will prioritize.

Goal: after the deep-dive we want a short mutual action plan (MAP) showing milestones to proof-of-concept (demo + security signoff + contract).

Available times: Thu 22 Jul 14:00-16:00 ET or Fri 23 Jul 10:00-12:00 ET.

Hey Daniel / Alice  quick technical follow-up as promised. Below are concrete details we typically provide customers in the deep-dive; happy to expand any section on the call.

1) RBAC & least privilege
- We provide a first-class RBAC model with predefined roles (viewer, analyst, dev, infra-admin, support-readonly, support-elevated). Roles are additive; customers can create custom roles via the Console or API.
- Role enforcement is at the service layer: every API call is checked against the user's effective permissions with no shared admin credentials.
- We can export a CSV role matrix (attached: rbac-matrix.csv) mapping our roles to your internal personas.

2) SSO / provisioning
- SAML 2.0 SSO and SCIM provisioning supported for automatic user sync and group management. Provisioning events are logged.

3) Support access & break-glass
- Support access is JIT (just-in-time) with an approval workflow: customer approver(s) are notified and must sign off via the Console or an auditable API.
- Duration: access is time-bound (default 1 hour) and requires re-approval to extend.
- All actions during break-glass sessions are fully logged and retained in an append-only audit log. We also support optional session recording/streaming for sensitive environments.
- Runbook attached: support-breakglass-runbook.md  outlines step-by-step and Slack/email approval options.

4) Encryption & BYOK
- We support Bring-Your-Own-Key with AWS KMS and Google Cloud KMS  keys remain in your KMS and Redwood never stores unencrypted key material.
- Data at rest is encrypted; we also support envelope encryption and per-tenant key rotation.

5) Data residency & retention
- Deployment regions: us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1. Data can be pinned to a region for both primary storage and backups.
- Retention: token-level logs default to 90 days; full request/response archives can be configured from 30 days to 7 years depending on your contract. Deletion is performed via a documented TTL process and scrubbed from hot storage; we provide a deletion certificate on request.

6) Audit evidence & compliance artifacts
- SOC 2 Type II report (redacted) is available  Marissa attached the executive report.
- We perform annual penetration testing; summary available and detailed findings can be shared under NDA.

If helpful I can run through the role matrix and break-glass flow in the tech deep-dive and show the Console screens for approvals and the audit log.

Cheers,

Dev Patel
